plays.story: Original Dark Sun creators are officially updating their Dragon Kings setting for 5E, reviving one of TTRPG's most beloved post-apocalyptic worlds

angles.bizzal-games: "Dark Sun's Dragon Kings Return: A DM's Guide to Running Athas in 5E" — break down how the classic defiler/preserver magic system, psionics, and survival-brutal ecology translate into 5E mechanics, with practical conversion tips for tables wanting that grim desert vibe.
angles.itsalreadywritten: "The World That Refused to Die: Dragon Kings' Return to Dark Sun's Untold Lore" — a narrative deep-dive on the setting's legendary worldbuilding (sorcerer-kings, dying sun, slave revolts) and what its original creators are choosing to preserve vs. reinvent for a new generation of readers/players.

plays.story: D&D: Warlock reveals first gameplay footage, confirmed to be set in Ravenloft

angles.bizzal-games: "What D&D: Warlock's Ravenloft Gameplay Just Taught Us About Running Gothic Horror at the Table" — mine the footage for encounter design, fog/mist mechanics, and dread-building tricks GMs can steal for their own Curse of Strahd sessions.
angles.itsalreadywritten: "Strahd's Realm, Reimagined: How D&D: Warlock Reinterprets Ravenloft's Gothic Legacy" — a lore-focused look at how the game's take on the Demiplane of Dread stacks up against decades of Ravenloft fiction and source material.

plays.story: This week's RPG crowdfunding roundup features Crows, Cypher, Monsters of Rend World, and more indie campaigns worth backer attention

angles.bizzal-games: "Backer's Radar: The Crunchiest Systems in This Week's RPG Crowdfunding Slate" — rank the campaigns by mechanical innovation (Cypher-adjacent systems, Monsters of Rend World's creature-building rules) for GMs hunting new toolkits.
angles.itsalreadywritten: "Worlds Worth Funding: The Standout Settings in This Week's TTRPG Crowdfunding Wave" — spotlight the strongest lore and setting concepts among Crows and Rend World, framed as 'stories you can help write into existence.'

plays.story: AI-generated bug reports triggered an emergency warning for Bitcoin Lightning node operators, exposing a new AI-driven attack surface in crypto infrastructure

angles.itsalreadypriced: "AI Just Sent Bitcoin Lightning Node Operators Into Emergency Mode — What It Means for Your BTC Stack" — explain the market/investor angle: how infra scares like this ripple into custody risk, exchange liquidity, and why traders watching the $79k-$83k range should care about node-level vulnerabilities.
angles.itsalreadywhen: "When AI Writes Your Vulnerability Reports: The Lightning Network Emergency Patch, Explained" — dig into the security mechanics: how AI-generated bug reports created false urgency (or real risk), what it reveals about AI's growing role in vuln disclosure pipelines, and lessons for infra teams bracing for more of this.
